tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__start_session
tools.description:
Start a separate Claude Code session for a task while you stay with the user (when: see "Starting other sessions"). `initiation` says who wants it: "user_asked" starts it now and returns its id; "offer" is for a task the user named in their latest message (new work here, or "suggest / split off / make a task or session for X"): called with a title alone, it shows a "New session" / "Do it here" card and WAITS for their answer, so it must be the only call in that message (no update_plan, no other tool); the result then tells you to carry on here, or to send the brief with proposal_id so the session starts; "own_initiative" is for work you propose yourself that the user has not told you to do — something you noticed, or the follow-up your own answer or work turned up (when your reply calls work a follow-up or a separate PR, propose it here rather than only saying so); the user sees a card and nothing runs until they start it, by clicking it or by telling you (then call this again with just proposal_id).
"user_asked" and "own_initiative" both need a `prompt` — the brief: the task, the files or area, what done looks like — and the call is refused without it; `background` does not stand in for it. Only an "offer" is a title alone.
context: "fork" = this whole conversation + your `prompt`. "fresh" (default) = your `prompt` + `background` only, so `background` is required too, at least 80 characters.
Checkout here ("fresh" only): use_worktree false = shares this checkout and can edit it (in a worktree session its branch and PR too: never for work that ends in a branch or PR of its own or belongs in another repository); true = its own worktree (the default when this session is in one).
Elsewhere ("fresh", user_asked only, when the user named the place): `cwd`, `target` "ssh" + `host`, `environment` or `preset`; list_start_targets lists the valid names.
Right before calling, write its bold title line and one sentence on what it will do; it has started only once this returns saying so. Never wait for it or poll.

schema.description:

"user_asked" and "own_initiative" both need a `prompt` — the brief: the task, the files or area, what done looks like — and the call is refused without it; `background` does not stand in for it. Only an "offer" is a title alone.
context: "fork" = this whole conversation + your `prompt`. "fresh" (default) = your `prompt` + `background` only, so `background` is required too, at least 80 characters.
Checkout here ("fresh" only): use_worktree false = shares this checkout and can edit it (in a worktree session its branch and PR too: never for work that ends in a branch or PR of its own or belongs in another repository); true = its own worktree (the default when this session is in one).
Elsewhere ("fresh", user_asked only, when the user named the place): `cwd`, `target` "ssh" + `host`, `environment` or `preset`; list_start_targets lists the valid names.

initiation.description: "user_asked": the user asked in words for separate, parallel or background work, or told you to start this piece — it starts now. "offer": a task the user named in their latest message (new work for this session, or one they asked you to suggest, split off or make a session for) — the user is asked first and the call waits for their answer; send only title with it (the brief follows, with proposal_id, if they choose New session). "own_initiative": work you propose yourself that the user has not told you to do — something you noticed, or the follow-up your own answer or work turned up; it waits as a proposal card until the user starts it; never for a task the user's message tells you to do. Required unless proposal_id is set.

proposal_id.description: Start a proposal the user told you to start, exactly as proposed: its task_id and nothing else (wake_when_done may accompany a local one). To change it, dismiss_task it and start a new session.

title.description: Under 60 chars; names the task. Shown on the row or card. Required unless proposal_id is set.

prompt.description: The brief: the task, the files or area, what done looks like. Required for "user_asked" and "own_initiative" — the call is refused without it, and `background` does not stand in for it; an "offer" leaves it out (the card shows the user's own message) and you send it with proposal_id once they choose New session.

context.description: "fresh" (default) or "fork" — see the tool description. A "fork" from a worktree session gets a fresh worktree, normally cut from your branch tip (commit first; uncommitted edits stay here); from a plain checkout it shares the folder.

background.description: Required with "fresh", besides `prompt`: at least 80 characters of overall goal, decisions and constraints so far, how this piece fits — for someone who has not seen this conversation. Ignored for "fork".

wake_when_done.description: Once this session (and any sibling still working) ends its turn, or fails to start (unless it waits at a prompt the user answers there, its folder was never opened in Claude Desktop, or the user started, stopped or archived it), and you are idle, the app continues you, whether or not this is set. true also continues you if this session never gets its task some other way, such as a brief that is not sent; default false; not with own_initiative; ignored with target "cloud", which never continues you.

name.description: Optional short handle for the session ([a-z0-9-], ≤24), e.g. "cli-cleanup". Linked sessions and plan steps refer to it by this name; derived from the title when omitted.

use_worktree.description: "fresh" only (rejected with "fork"). false = shares this session's checkout and can edit it (in a worktree session: its worktree, branch and PR, so never for work that ends in a branch or PR of its own or belongs in another repository); not accepted from a session set up to move from the user's checkout into a worktree with EnterWorktree (before or after it moves), one working in a worktree on an SSH host, or one whose worktree was given back. At another place named by `cwd`, `host` or `preset`, false = that folder as it is. true = its own git worktree. Omitted: the same folder when this session works in a plain folder and has never had a worktree (its own, a shared one, or one it will enter later); otherwise its own worktree. Omitted with `preset` or `host`, or with `cwd` from a session on an SSH host: the default set on that preset or SSH connection instead.

model.description: "fresh" only, optional: a cheaper model id for mechanical or read-only pieces (e.g. a Sonnet or Haiku id). Same family or cheaper than yours; anything higher is ignored. Omit to inherit yours.

target.description: "fresh" only. "local" (default) = where this session runs. "cloud" = run it as a cloud session (keeps going when this computer sleeps). Needs the repository on GitHub and a cloud environment — the app checks and tells the user if it cannot, and the task then stays as a card for them to start. It starts from this session's pushed branch when it runs in a worktree, else the repository's default branch. model/effort/use_worktree/cwd/source_branch do not apply. Only when the user asks for the cloud. "ssh" = on the SSH connection named by host (or by a preset).

host.description: With target "ssh": the name of one of the user's saved SSH connections (as list_start_targets reports it) — never a raw hostname, user or key. The app connects as the user configured it and may ask them to sign in.

cwd.description: The folder the session works in, when it is not this project: an absolute (or ~/) path on the host it will run on — this computer, this session's host, or the SSH connection named by host (default there: the connection's folder). Must exist; if the user has not trusted it yet the app asks them first. "fresh" only.

environment.description: With target "cloud": the name or id of one of the user's cloud environments (list_start_targets lists them); omitted = the default one. Self-hosted environments and runner pools need the user's own click and are refused, and so is an environment that cannot run this project's repository.

source_branch.description: The existing local branch the new worktree is cut from. Default in this project: this session's base branch (the one picked when it started, or the one its worktree was cut from). If the session has none and either it runs on an SSH host or its project folder is itself a git worktree or submodule, the folder's current commit. Otherwise, the repository's default branch, or the folder's current commit if that is unknown. Only for a session that gets its own worktree (use_worktree true, or the place's default); not with target "cloud".

branch_name.description: A short slug for the new worktree's branch (the app adds the user's branch prefix and a suffix). Only with a worktree.

preset.description: The name of one of the user's saved session presets on this computer: it names the place itself (a folder here or an SSH connection and folder — do not pass host or cwd with it) and brings model, effort and worktree defaults plus its saved environment variables; use_worktree/model/effort override those. Cloud and Remote Control presets are not available here.

effort.description: "fresh" only, optional: reasoning effort at or below yours. Omit to inherit.

permission_mode.description: Optional, local starts only: the permission mode it starts in — this session's own or a lower one (omit to inherit it). A higher mode, or one the app does not offer here, is refused; raising a session is set_session_permission_mode's card to show.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work: the user follows your progress by it and will never ask for it, so it is part of the task. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

scope.description: Required with items: "first_task", "continuation" or "new_task" (see the tool description). Omit on advance / done / start updates.

content.description: The step, as a short imperative phrase (≤7 words).

session.description: When you delegated this step to a session you started: that session's short name (from start_session's result). The app shows its live state on the step.

items.description: The whole plan, in order (1–12 steps); replaces the previous list. Use on the first call and whenever the plan changes.

advance.description: true: the in_progress step is done and the next pending step starts (the cheap, usual update).

done.description: 1-based numbers of steps just completed (out-of-order updates).

start.description: 1-based number of the step now in progress (with done, for out-of-order updates).

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: propose it and call this.

The result says which case below applies. When the box shows your question, it ends your turn: write no text after this call, since the recap and question say what the user needs and your work above holds the detail. Otherwise your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, with any question the box did not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label and message are the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status.

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead, an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Fix 2 instead", "Not now": a button, not a sentence; the detail goes in message. No "@", no leading / or !. Ignored for an app action (the app's own label is used).

message.description: For a reply: what the click sends, up to 300 characters of plain text — no "@" anywhere, no leading / or !. Omit when the label is the whole message.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
schema.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

name.description: Tool name (e.g. computer, navigate, find, form_input, read_page). browser_batch cannot be nested. A tabs_create's new tabId is only returned when the batch ends — load that tab in a later call.

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

actions.description: List of tool calls to execute sequentially. Example: [{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"left_click","ref":"ref_12"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"type","text":"hello"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"screenshot"}}]

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

---
paths:
  - "frontend/src/pages/Annotate.tsx"
  - "frontend/src/components/annotate/**"
  - "frontend/src/utils/describeEvent.ts"
---

# Annotate page (manual labelling)

- **Reads and writes labels only:** `useEvents(fightId, { source: 'label' })` plus `createEvent`/`updateEvent`/`deleteEvent`, all of which the backend scopes to `source='label'`. Point `events` and `spans` (any non-point kind) are derived from that one result with `useMemo`. Annotate opens only when `state` is `labeling_in_progress`.
- **Every modal needs a keyboard guard.** Mirror the modal's open state into a ref and check it in the global keydown handler, the way `endOpenRef` and `confirmDeleteRef` work. Otherwise keys keep writing label events and spans underneath the overlay.

## Point events (palette and keys)
- Each `ToolItem` in `annotate/taxonomy.ts` `TOOL_GROUPS` defines its palette button, shortcut and legend entry together. Add new tools there.
- **Hand strikes** (`hasTarget`): the plain key means head and Shift+key means body. Read `e.code` plus `e.shiftKey`, not `e.key`, because Shift changes `e.key` on a US layout.
- **Kicks** carry a `fixedTarget`.
- `successForAction` returns `true` only for outcome actions (`knockdown`, `takedown_landed`). Strikes get `null`: landed/missed is deferred, so never default a strike to landed.
- **Create payloads have no `description`.** `ToolItem.text()` builds only the toast. `describeEvent` rebuilds text through `ACTION_TO_TOOL`, a reverse index over `TOOL_GROUPS`. Only `fight_end`, built in `confirmFightEnd`, sends a description.
- `Annotate.tsx` builds one `describe(e)` closure (fighter names plus this fight's `corner_swap` spans) and passes it through `AnnotationPanel` to both `AnnotationList` and `AnnotationTimeline`. Never read `e.description` there. That way, marking a swap instantly corrects strikes that were already logged.
- **Fight-state marks** (`W`/`F`/`G`) are change points, not spans. The timeline's State lane pairs each mark with the next one. In the UI the last mark runs to the end of the timeline, but `ai/eval/labels_db.py` ends it at the end of its round.

## Spans (`O` and `P` keys)
- **`round`** spans are seeded server-side from `rounds` on first fetch. They show as draggable blocks in the Rounds lane, and edge-drag → `onUpdateSpan` → `PUT frame/end_frame`.
- **`K` (or the Rounds lane `+`) adds a round** at the playhead: it splits the round span it falls in, or else runs to the next round. After any round add or delete, `renumberRounds` rewrites `value` to the span's 1-based order, because eval and export read `value` as the round number.
- **`corner_swap` and `excluded`** are start/end toggles. `openSpanRef` holds the in-flight id for each kind: the first press creates the span with `end_frame=null`, and the second press `PUT`s `end_frame`. An open span draws dashed up to the playhead.

## Finish and re-edit
- **Finish Labeling** is gated server-side: it returns 409 until every round has a confirmed `round` label. Don't duplicate the check client-side. On success it returns to Player with `replace`, so Back can't land on Annotate's "already labeled" screen.
- **Re-editing** (`isEditingLabels` = `labeling_in_progress && labeled_at !== null`) shows the "Edit labels" title. `needsRoundReview` also checks `labeled_at`, so the unverified-rounds banner doesn't come back during an edit. The "already labeled" screen offers the same **Edit labels** action.

# frontend/ — React + TypeScript + Vite

**Pages** (`src/pages/`):
- `FightList`: library and upload, updated live via the SSE stream.
- `Player`: fight review.
- `Annotate`: hand labelling.
- `TrainingDataQA` (`/training-data`).
- `PipelineAccuracy` (`/accuracy`).
- `Library`: legacy.
- `Users` (`/users`, admin): roles and access.
- `SignIn`: rendered by `AuthProvider` in place of the app while signed out.

Data access goes through `services/api.ts` plus one hook per resource in `hooks/`. Every call uses `apiFetch`, which adds the `/api` prefix and reloads the page on a 401. `<video src>` and `EventSource` must use `videoUrl()` and `FIGHT_STREAM_URL`, and they authenticate through the same-origin session cookie.

**Auth:** `AuthProvider` renders the app only after `/api/auth/me` answers. Use `useAuth().can(role)` to hide controls and `RequireRole` to guard routes. Both are cosmetic, because the backend enforces roles.

**Page-specific rules load when you open matching files:**
- `.claude/rules/frontend-player.md`
- `.claude/rules/frontend-annotate.md`
- `.claude/rules/frontend-training-data-qa.md`

## Dev server
`vite.config.ts` proxies `/api` to `127.0.0.1:8000`. Every backend route lives under `/api`, so client routes never collide with it. Never add a client route under `/api`.

## Conventions
- **Frame numbers:** use `Math.floor(currentTime * fps) + 1` with `fight.fps`, and step frames with `delta / fps` seconds. Never hardcode fps.
- **Event text** comes from `utils/describeEvent.ts`, and category, colour and icon come from `utils/eventTaxonomy.ts`, keyed on `action`. Never parse or display `description`. Only `fight_end` has one.
- **Strike attribution** (`utils/liveStats.ts`) uses `fighter_id` for predictions (matched against `fights.red_fighter_id`) and `corner` for labels, never text.
- **Corner-swap correction is display-only**, via `utils/cornerSwap.ts`'s `isFrameSwapped`. It is used for box colour in `FighterOverlay` and for fighter names in `describeEvent`. Never write a swapped corner back.
- **`useFighterFrames(fightId)`** with no range downloads the whole fight's keypoints, tens of MB. That's fine for Player and Annotate, which scrub anywhere. Anything that needs only a few frames must pass `{start_frame, end_frame}`.
- **Mock data:** fighter profiles, stats, pace and recent form are hardcoded in `src/mocks/fightMock.ts`. `TODO_BACKEND_DATA.md` lists the API each one needs.
- **Badge colours:** purpose and other badges must not reuse the red/blue corner colours or the error/warning colours, because a red badge reads as "red corner". See `PURPOSE_COLORS` in `types/Fight.ts`.

## Design
The look is shared with `landing/`. Tokens and shared classes live in `src/index.css`; components style inline with those tokens.
- **Orange (`--accent`) means the brand, a screen's primary action, or the AI** (the `ai_labeled` badge, model scores and prediction charts on Accuracy). Selection, focus, playheads, progress bars and human-labelled counts use ink (`--text-primary`), so orange never sits beside the red corner like a third fighter.
- **Red and blue mean corners only, and text never wears a corner colour.** Put a swatch next to ink text instead, so a name stays readable and the colour stays a mark.
- **Type:** Archivo everywhere. Headings use `.font-display` (condensed, heavy) and are written in sentence case. Every stat, count and score uses `.font-num` (JetBrains Mono), so digits line up.
- **Shape:** controls 6px (`--r-ctl`), tiles 8px, panels 12px. No pills, and no glow shadows.
- **Don't change a data colour by eye.** Corners, the state trio, `--warn`, statuses and `PURPOSE_COLORS` were measured against each other; run the dataviz skill's `validate_palette.js` before touching one. The app's corner blue stays `#60a5fa` (the landing page uses `#4f93ea`), because the darker blue sits even closer to `--state-ground`.

## Upload (`UploadDialog`)
**AI annotation** always sends `purpose='ai_labeled'`. **Self-annotate** shows a purpose radio group (`training_data` / `reference`) with **no default**, and Upload stays disabled until one is picked. The gate is deliberate: the training and evaluation sets must never be split by inattention. `uploadFight()` sends `purpose` as the only track selector.

## Deleting a fight
`DELETE /fights/{id}` is irreversible: it kills the pipeline, unlinks the video, and cascades every event. All entry points go through `ConfirmDialog`:
- **`Player.tsx`** is the only place to delete a healthy fight. Keep two things:
  - `videoRef.current.pause()` before the request, because the `<video>` is still streaming the file being unlinked.
  - `navigate('/', { replace: true })` afterwards.
- **`Annotate.tsx`** has a header button. See the Annotate rule for the keyboard guard every modal needs.
- **`FightList.tsx`** shows delete only on `failed`/`invalid` rows (a delete-and-re-upload recovery path) and `queued` rows (cancelling a job no worker has claimed). It uses one dialog outside the `.map`, driven by `pendingDelete`.

- **`K` (or the Rounds lane `+`) adds a round** at the playhead: it splits the round span it falls in, or else runs to the next round. After any round add or delete, `renumberRounds` rewrites `value` to the span's 1-based order, because eval and export read `value` as the round number.
- **`corner_swap` and `excluded`** are start/end toggles. `openSpanRef` holds the in-flight id for each kind: the first press creates the span with `end_frame=null`, and the second press `PUT`s `end_frame`. An open span draws dashed up to the playhead.

## Finish and re-edit
- **Finish Labeling** is gated server-side: it returns 409 until every round has a confirmed `round` label. Don't duplicate the check client-side. On success it returns to Player with `replace`, so Back can't land on Annotate's "already labeled" screen.
- **Re-editing** (`isEditingLabels` = `labeling_in_progress && labeled_at !== null`) shows the "Edit labels" title. `needsRoundReview` also checks `labeled_at`, so the unverified-rounds banner doesn't come back during an edit. The "already labeled" screen offers the same **Edit labels** action.

content.content:
3:Serves fights, rounds, fighter frames, events and eval runs from PostgreSQL, and spawns and tracks the AI pipeline as a subprocess in the `ai/` venv. Routes live in `app/api/routes/`, SQLAlchemy models and Pydantic schemas in `app/models/`, and logic in `app/services/`.
5:Run it from `backend/` with `uvicorn app.main:app --reload`. It uses `backend/.venv` (see `backend/.envrc`), not the root `.venv`, which belongs to the pipeline. Install `requirements.txt` into `backend/.venv`, or the auto-reload dies on an `ImportError` and every request hangs.
10:- `AI_DIR` and `AI_PYTHON` override the ai venv that `pipeline_runner.py` spawns into. They default to `../ai` and `../.venv/bin/python`.
26:- **`GET /auth/dev-login?role=…` is the only way around Google**, for Claude sessions and curl (usage is in the root CLAUDE.md). It creates a normal session for a synthetic `dev-<role>@fightai.local` user, so every role check still runs. It resets that user's role and active flag on each call, and answers 404 to non-loopback clients because uvicorn may be bound to `0.0.0.0`. Labels created under it are stamped with the dev email as `labeler`.
27:- **A role-gated route that accepts a large body must not declare `File()`/`Form()` params.** FastAPI parses the body before it runs dependencies, so a viewer could stream a whole video to disk before the 403. `upload_fight` reads `request.form()` itself.
44:- **`purpose`** is set only by `POST /fights/upload` and validated against `FIGHT_PURPOSES`. Only `ai_labeled` runs the full pipeline; the labelling purposes get `skip_events`. No API changes it afterwards (use a manual `UPDATE`), and the pipeline's upsert must never add it to its `SET` list.
49:  1. `POST /fights/upload` creates the row at `validating`, stamped with `uploaded_by` (the signed-in admin), and calls `pipeline_runner.run_validation_async()`.
50:  2. That runs `eval.cli video --fight-id` in the ai venv.
53:- **`DELETE /fights/{id}`** kills the running pipeline or validator, unlinks the video, and deletes the row (child rows cascade).
54:  - It only signals a pid whose command line matches `pipeline_runner._AI_ENTRYPOINTS`, so a recycled OS pid is never killed. **Any new AI-venv job spawned from `pipeline_runner.py` must add its marker there.**

content.text:
You can now delete a fight state in self-annotate mode: click its segment in the timeline's **State** lane to select it, then press Delete (Backspace on a Mac).

**What was wrong:** the State lane drew each segment as a plain block you couldn't click. So although the Delete key already removes whatever is selected, there was no way to select a state.

**The change** is all in [AnnotationTimeline.tsx](frontend/src/components/annotate/AnnotationTimeline.tsx):
- Each state segment is now a button. Clicking it jumps the playhead to where the state starts and selects it, with the same white ring a selected strike gets.
- Deleting removes that state change, so the state before it now runs on in its place.
- Hovering a selected segment shows "Delete to remove", as strikes already do.

I tested it in the browser on fight 68. I added a temporary Clinch state, clicked it and pressed Backspace. It was deleted from the database and disappeared from the timeline, so the fight's labels are back to how they were. The code type-checks.

Postgres briefly stopped accepting connections while I was testing, then came back on its own; this change didn't cause that.

I also added a `backend` entry to [.claude/launch.json](.claude/launch.json) so the API server can be started from the app's preview. Nothing is committed.

content.content:
# backend/ — FastAPI service

Serves fights, rounds, fighter frames, events and eval runs from PostgreSQL, and spawns and tracks the AI pipeline as a subprocess in the `ai/` venv. Routes live in `app/api/routes/`, SQLAlchemy models and Pydantic schemas in `app/models/`, and logic in `app/services/`.

Run it from `backend/` with `uvicorn app.main:app --reload`. It uses `backend/.venv` (see `backend/.envrc`), not the root `.venv`, which belongs to the pipeline. Install `requirements.txt` into `backend/.venv`, or the auto-reload dies on an `ImportError` and every request hangs.

## Env
- `DATABASE_URL` is required.
- `VIDEO_BASE_DIR` resolves relative `video_path`s, and uploads create `fight_videos/` inside it.
- `AI_DIR` and `AI_PYTHON` override the ai venv that `pipeline_runner.py` spawns into. They default to `../ai` and `../.venv/bin/python`.
- `KEEP_VIDEO_ON_DELETE=1` (dev only) makes `DELETE /fights/{id}` keep the video file. Set it when you test deletes by hand.
- `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`, `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` and `SESSION_SECRET` are required; startup fails without them.
- `PUBLIC_BASE_URL` (required) is the origin the browser sees: `http://localhost:5173` in dev. The OAuth redirect URI (`<PUBLIC_BASE_URL>/api/auth/callback`, which must be registered in Google Cloud) and the cookie's Secure flag both derive from it, because the Vite proxy rewrites `Host`.
- `ADMIN_EMAILS` (comma-separated) makes those addresses admin **when their row is created** on first sign-in. It is not re-applied later.
- `DEV_LOGIN=1` (local only) mounts `GET /auth/dev-login`. Startup fails if it is set while `PUBLIC_BASE_URL` is anything but `http://localhost` or `http://127.0.0.1`, so it can never be live on a deployed instance.
- `FRONTEND_DIST` (prod only) serves the built SPA from this origin, with an `index.html` fallback for client routes.
- `PIPELINE_DISPATCH=queue` (prod only, set in `deploy/Dockerfile`) is inherited by the validator subprocess, which then leaves a valid upload `queued` instead of spawning `main.py`. The server has no torch.
- `SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_SECURITY`, `SMTP_USERNAME`, `SMTP_PASSWORD` and `MAIL_FROM` (optional) turn on email notifications (`services/email_service.py`). With `SMTP_HOST` unset, emails are only logged, which is what dev and tests want.

## Auth
Route paths elsewhere in this file omit the `/api` prefix.
- **`app/main.py` mounts every router under `/api` with `Depends(current_user)`**, except `/api/auth/*`. `tests/test_auth.py` fails if a route escapes it.
- **Every write route declares its minimum role** with `require_role("labeller")` or `require_role("admin")` in its decorator. Reads need only a session. Add the new route to the role matrix in `tests/test_auth.py`.
- **The cookie holds only the user id.** `current_user` re-reads the `users` row on every request, so a role change or disable applies immediately.
- **Users are disabled (`is_active=false`), never deleted.** Auto-join would bring a deleted user straight back as a viewer. `PATCH /users/{id}` refuses self-edits, which guarantees an admin always remains.

Never read `e.description` there. That way, marking a swap instantly corrects strikes that were already logged.

- **Fight-state marks** (`W`/`F`/`G`) are change points, not spans. The timeline's State lane pairs each mark with the next one. In the UI the last mark runs to the end of the timeline, but `ai/eval/labels_db.py` ends it at the end of its round.

+- A State-lane segment *is* its starting mark: clicking selects that mark (Delete removes it), the left edge drags its `frame` and the right edge drags the next mark's. Drags clamp between neighbouring marks, so the order never changes.
- **`round`** spans are seeded server-side from `rounds` on first fetch. They show as draggable blocks in the Rounds lane, and edge-drag → `onUpdateSpan` → `PUT frame/end_frame`.
`services/event_service.py` implements these. See the root CLAUDE.md for the `source`/`kind` model.
- `GET /fights/{id}/events/` returns every row unless filtered, so callers pass `source`. The first `source=label` fetch for a fight also seeds `kind='round'` labels from `rounds`.
- `POST …/events/` always writes `source='label'` and stamps `labeler` with the signed-in user's email. `FightEventCreate` has neither field, so a client can't spoof a prediction or another labeller.
-- `PUT …/events/{eid}` edits `frame`, `end_frame` or `value` on **label spans only**. It returns 404 for predictions and for `kind='point'`: points are create and delete only.

+- `PUT …/events/{eid}` edits `frame`, `end_frame` or `value` on **label spans**, and only `frame` on a label `state_*` point (the State lane drags it). It returns 404 for predictions and every other point, because a strike that moved would no longer match its QA verdict.

- `PUT …/events/{eid}/verify` sets `is_verified` on **label points only**, the opposite scope. It returns 409 when setting true or false on a fight whose purpose isn't `training_data`. Clearing to null is always allowed.

- `PUT …/events/{eid}/reclassify` (Training Data QA) rewrites `action`, `target` and `success` on **label points only**. It deliberately leaves `corner` and `is_verified` alone. It has no purpose check: the backend stores whatever columns the frontend's `reclassifyPayload()` computes.
- `DELETE …/events/{eid}` works on label rows only and returns 404 for anything else.

content.text:
You can now resize fight states by dragging the edges of their boxes in the State lane, the same way you resize rounds. Each box runs from one state change to the next, so:

- **Left edge:** moves where this state starts.
- **Right edge:** moves where the next state starts, so the box and the one after it change size together. The last box has no right edge, since it runs to the end of the fight.
- **Limits:** an edge can't be dragged past the state change on either side, so states never swap order.
- **Clicking** a box still selects it, and Delete still removes it.

**Backend change:** the API used to refuse any edit to a single-moment event. It now lets you move the frame of a fight-state mark and nothing else. Strikes still can't be moved, so a QA verdict always refers to the frame that was checked. I added two tests for this. The existing event tests were already failing before my change because their test setup didn't create the `users` table, so I fixed that too. All 81 backend tests pass now.

**Tested in the browser** on fight 68. I added two test states and dragged one from frame 9000 to 6927, and the new frame was saved. I then dragged it far to the left and it stopped at 3646, one frame after the state before it. I deleted both test states afterwards. Your two states (frames 1 and 3645) were never moved.

content.text:
I've fixed the jump: when you let go, the boundary now stays where you dropped it.

**Cause:** on release, the timeline stopped using your drag position straight away, but the new position only appeared once the server confirmed the save. For that moment the boundary snapped back to where it started, then jumped to its new place.

**Fix:** the new position now shows as soon as you let go. The save runs in the background, and if it fails the boundary moves back and you get an error message. Round edges had the same jump, so they're fixed too. The change is in `updateSpan` in [Annotate.tsx](frontend/src/pages/Annotate.tsx).

**Check:** in the browser I slowed the save down to 0.8 seconds and dragged a test state. The boundary stayed where I released it the whole time. Before the fix it would have jumped back about 56 px first. I deleted the test state afterwards.

Your CLINCH state on fight 68 is now at frame 8628 rather than 3645. My test only touched its own mark, so I assume that was your drag. Nothing is committed.
